locator: Executive Summary, Water Production (printed p. 10); Water Production (into Distribution System) table (printed p. 45)
shows: The Interim Third-Party Manager reports the average daily water production into the distribution system of the two plants for each quarter. For the last four quarters it was 40.4 MGD (Q3 2025), 35.9 MGD (Q4 2025), 37.0 MGD (Q1 2026) and 35.1 MGD (Q2 2026); over the 365 days from July 2025 to June 2026 that is 37.1 MGD (derived, each quarter weighted by its days). Production was 47 to 56 MGD a quarter in 2023. The report estimates the water loss at about 50% (17 mgd), against more than 65% (35 mgd) in October 2023.
limits: Quarterly means of plant output, which includes the water lost from the pipes: the report gives no highest day. Production falls each year as leaks are repaired, so a figure from an earlier year overstates the present need. The loss is an estimate.

locator: Design Capacity Sheet of December 8, 2021: Fewell design capacity (p. 2) and O B Curtis treatment capacity (pp. 2-4); inspection report comment 7
shows: The Mississippi State Department of Health rates the two plants of the City of Jackson in its November 2021 survey. It sets a maximum treatment capacity of 20 MGD at J.H. Fewell. At O.B. Curtis, each side, conventional and membrane, was rated at 25 MGD; in 2021 the department credited only 16.8 MGD to each side, for the four filters and four membrane trains in service, 33.6 MGD in all. The rated capacities sum to 70 MGD and the credited ones to 53.6 MGD (derived). With the service pumps that were working, the design capacity of the two plants was 34 + 38 = 72 MGD.
limits: A state survey of November 2021, before the plant failures of August 2022 and the repairs that JXN Water has made since 2023; the credited capacities changed as filters, trains and pumps came back. The 20 MGD at Fewell is a limit that the department set from turbidity data; the plant averaged 22.3 MGD in the third quarter of 2025, so that limit has changed since.

locator: Design Capacity Sheet of December 8, 2021: Fewell design capacity (p. 2), O B Curtis design capacity (p. 3) and total system design capacity (p. 4)
shows: The survey counts 13.8 MG of storage at J.H. Fewell (a 3.8 MG clearwell and two 5 MG ground tanks), a 10 MG clearwell at O.B. Curtis, and 7.75 MG of elevated storage in nine tanks: 31.55 MG in all (derived). It leaves out three elevated tanks: the 1.0 MG Byram tank, offline since November 2020, and the 0.2 MG Suncrest and 1.0 MG Elaine tanks, which were empty on the day of the survey.
limits: A count of November 2021. The 31.55 MG leaves out 2.2 MG of tanks that were offline or empty then; with them the total is 33.75 MG (derived). The survey also says that the plants could not pump enough water to keep all elevated tanks full. The figures are total capacities, not the volume that operators can draw down.
